candidates.abstract: The miniKanren and Relational Programming Workshop brings together researchers, implementors, and users of the miniKanren family of relational programming languages, including miniKanren, microKanren, core.logic, OCanren, Guanxi, and related systems. The workshop focuses on the design, implementation, and application of miniKanren-like languages, as well as new techniques and tools for relational programming. These proceedings collect the eleven accepted papers presented at the Seventh miniKanren and Relational Programming Workshop.

contribution.en: Proceedings of the miniKanren and relational programming workshop.
contribution.zh: miniKanren与关系式编程研讨会的论文集。

candidates.title: Proceedings of the Seventh miniKanren and Relational Programming Workshop (miniKanren 2025)

recommendations.abstract: Wider vector/SIMD lanes multiply compute throughput, but cache improvements remain challenging. We identify L1 data cache capacity as the most impactful parameter for performance and efficiency. L1 capacity is constrained by pipeline coupling and latency requirements; private L2 offers an order of magnitude more capacity but is inaccessible from software. This work proposes CacheFlex, an ISA and microarchitecture co-design that enables software-managed, direct access to private L2 SRAM by allowing runtime conversion of parts of L2 into a scratchpad memory (SPM). Through a lightweight ISA extension, software explicitly controls data placement and lifetime within the L2. CacheFlex integrates into an out-of-order pipeline with cross-domain memory consistency and OS context-switch support, with merely 2.02% area overhead relative to the L2 in a post-layout 12 nm implementation. We prototype CacheFlex based on the Armv8-A SVE ISA, model it in gem5, and evaluate it using optimized general matrix multiplication (GEMM) kernels with diverse model-derived shapes, FlashAttention-based fused attention, and full-layer workloads from LLaMA-3.2-1B and BERT-Base in the prefill phase. As the vector length (VL) scales from VL = 4 (512-bit) to VL = 16 (2048-bit), CacheFlex's kernel-level geometric-mean speedup and memory-subsystem energy reduction grow from 1.12x and 26% to 1.44x and 40%, respectively, bridging the widening gap between per-instruction data demand and memory performance. On full transformer layers combining CacheFlex with FlashAttention, the design delivers up to 1.78x speedup and 45% memory-subsystem energy savings (BERT-Base, sequence length T=4096, VL = 16; LLaMA-3.2-1B: 1.64x and 38%). CacheFlex is complementary to hardware prefetching, and its benefit grows as vector width and peak compute throughput increase for compute-intensive AI kernels.

contribution.en: ISA/microarchitecture co-design exposing private L2 as software-managed scratchpad for wide vectors.
contribution.zh: 通过ISA/微架构协同设计将私有L2暴露为面向宽向量的软件管理暂存器。

why_care.en: Directly informs compiler-managed memory for SIMD/vector code and accelerator co-design.
why_care.zh: 直接指导SIMD/向量代码的编译器管理内存与加速器协同设计。

recommendations.title: CacheFlex: Direct Software-Managed Access to Higher-Level Cache for Scalable Vector Support

recommendations.abstract: The layout algebra behind NVIDIA's CuTe library describes how tensor tiles map onto threads and memory. A layout is a shape with a stride for each entry, so a coordinate's address is the sum of its indices times their strides. As formalized by Shah and by Cecka, its central operations (e.g., composition, complement, division, product) are guarded by at least six interacting admissibility conditions. We show that this complexity is an artifact of a representational choice, not of the domain. We present a layout algebra in which every layout names the space its inputs and outputs live in: logical, physical, or thread-value indices. A layout into logical or thread-value space must be a bijection from its $N$ coordinates onto $[0,N)$. A layout into physical space must be alias-free: distinct coordinates land on distinct addresses, except under broadcast, where many threads read one value on purpose and the layout must mark where. Nothing maps out of a physical index. Composing $f$ with $g$ requires only that $f$'s range be exactly $g$'s flattened coordinate set. The index arithmetic can always be emitted naively: compute $f$, split the result by division and remainder into $g$'s coordinates, and apply $g$. Often the composite simplifies to a layout; we show that when it does, there is a coarsest such form, whose digits every other one refines, and we emit that. A warp's or thread's slice is a \emph{restriction}. A restricted layout is no longer composable, which forces the user to settle the whole view of a tile before taking slices. We validate the algebra by reproducing within it CuTe's operations, such as composition, complement, and division. We implement it in OCaml and use the implementation to rederive CuTe's atoms and usage patterns. The decision procedure is proved correct in Rocq.

contribution.en: Introduces a space-annotated layout algebra that simplifies composition, complement, and division for GPU tensor layouts.
contribution.zh: 提出一个带空间标注的布局代数，简化GPU张量布局的组合、补全与除法规则。

why_care.en: It directly relates to GPU kernel layout lowering, CuTe-like IRs, and verifiable compiler expression rewriting.
why_care.zh: 它直接关系到GPU内核布局lowering、CuTe类IR和可验证的编译器表达式重写。

recommendations.title: A Simplified Layout Algebra for GPU Kernels

recommendations.abstract: Modern attention workloads require diverse masking patterns whose boundaries depend on runtime metadata, yet efficient attention kernels natively support only a small set of patterns. Existing methods for supporting custom masks in these kernels face an expressiveness-efficiency trade-off. Predicate-based methods are expressive but incur substantial preprocessing and execution overhead, whereas interval-based methods execute efficiently but restrict expressiveness through a predefined interval count. We present CompileMask, which addresses this trade-off by connecting expressive mask specifications with efficient attention execution. We design a compiler that analyzes visibility rules during the offline stage and generates a mask-specific preprocess kernel. We further propose MaskSpec, a region-based DSL that lets users express these rules. During the online stage, the generated kernel reads batch metadata and produces a compact Execution Descriptor that lets the attention kernel efficiently check visibility by comparing element indices against precomputed endpoints. Experiments show that CompileMask achieves up to $3.8\times$ speedup over state-of-the-art methods.

contribution.en: Presents CompileMask/MaskSpec, a compiler approach that offline-generates attention-mask preprocess kernels and online descriptors.
contribution.zh: 提出CompileMask/MaskSpec，用编译器离线生成注意力掩码预处理内核和在线描述符。

why_care.en: It connects compilers, DSLs, and efficient GPU attention kernels, an adjacent code-generation problem.
why_care.zh: 它连接编译器、DSL与高效GPU注意力内核，属于相邻的代码生成问题。

recommendations.title: CompileMask: Bridging the Gap Between Expressiveness and Efficiency in Attention Masking

recommendations.abstract: GPU architecture research requires representative benchmarks that can execute on new designs. However, many vendor-tailored workloads and library kernels cannot run directly on research architectures because their implementations are closed-source or rely on programming models unsupported by the target architecture. Migrating existing kernels requires manual effort to adapt their implementations and validate their behavior. This creates a need to automate workload migration to target platforms. We present VortexSynth, a framework that uses profile-guided benchmark reconstruction to construct GPU benchmarks from reference workloads. Our workflow selects hot kernels through profiling, synthesizes implementations in the target programming language, verifies output equivalence, and measures profile differences using a translated proxy implementation. The resulting profile signature gap is supplied to an agent for iterative refinement. We evaluate the method on Vortex, an open-ISA GPGPU, using robotics as the application domain. All active kernel pairs pass both output-equivalence checks, and the case studies show that iterative refinement can reduce profile distance.

contribution.en: Profile-guided benchmark reconstruction synthesizes equivalent GPU kernels for open-ISA architectures.
contribution.zh: 以剖面引导的基准重构为开放ISA架构合成等价GPU内核。

why_care.en: Connects program synthesis and retargeting to GPU architecture benchmarking.
why_care.zh: 将程序合成与重定向编译连接到GPU体系结构基准评测。

recommendations.title: VortexSynth: Profile-guided benchmark reconstruction for GPU architecture research

recommendations.abstract: The growing diversity of domain-specific architectures and microarchitectural designs demands fast and accurate evaluation methods during early design stages. However, existing approaches suffer from a fundamental trade-off: high-level simulators offer speed but lack fidelity, while RTL-based tools provide accuracy at the cost of significant simulation overhead. This gap limits efficient pre-RTL microarchitecture exploration. Therefore, we propose Transaction-Pruned Cycle Simulation (TPCS), a novel modeling and simulation framework. It serves as a unified intermediate abstraction spanning microarchitecture modeling, cycle-accurate simulation, and synthesizable RTL implementation. TPCS organizes combinational logic as transaction-based function invocations and leverages host CPU control flow to naturally prune inactive logic, eliminating the need for explicit event scheduling or signal tracking. This enables cycle-accurate simulation with significantly improved performance. TPCS preserves structural correspondence with RTL and supports automatic generation of synthesizable designs. TPCS achieves 36$\times$-42$\times$ speedups over parallel Verilator on SMP systems and 3.4$\times$-7.2$\times$ over single-threaded Verilator on accelerators, with cycle-level waveform agreement on the evaluated traces. The generated RTL demonstrates comparable timing and area to handcrafted implementations, with relative changes of -4.7\% to +2.6\% in clock period and -3.3\% to +4.0\% in standard-cell area. By bridging the abstraction gap between high-level modeling and RTL design, TPCS enables a unified and agile pre-RTL workflow, allowing efficient microarchitecture exploration with both high performance and implementation fidelity.

contribution.en: Unifies cycle-level simulation and RTL generation via transaction-pruned host execution.
contribution.zh: 通过事务剪枝的主机执行统一周期级仿真与RTL生成。

why_care.en: Supports pre-RTL architecture exploration relevant to compiler-architecture co-design.
why_care.zh: 支持与编译-体系结构协同设计相关的前RTL架构探索。

recommendations.title: TPCS: A Cycle-Level Simulation Paradigm with Native Execution Semantics for RTL Modeling and Generation
